defects: A FIFTH DROP CHANNEL SURVIVES THE FIX, AND IT SITS UPSTREAM OF THE INVARIANT. The four buckets sum to `_meta_phd_n_texts_seen`, but `_n_seen` is itself incremented only AFTER _iter_per_document_clouds has yielded, and that generator `continue`s without yielding on three conditions -- blank/whitespace text, a zero-length encoding, and a missing hidden_states -- so those documents are in NO bucket and are invisible. Measured: feed 80 WikiText passages plus 20 whitespace-only documents at the production config and the task reports _meta_phd_n_texts_seen = 80 with buckets 56 + 8 + 16 + 0 = 80. The invariant HOLDS while 20 of 100 configured documents (20%) have disappeared with nothing recording them. The accounting is anchored to a post-drop count, which is the exact failure mode the four-bucket fix was written to close.

THE FIX MADE THE UNEQUAL-WEIGHT PROBLEM MEASURABLY WORSE, NOT BETTER, AND ITS OWN COMMENT STILL MISDESCRIBES IT. The comment says 'a 200-token document is fit on 4 points and a 512-token one on 12'. Measured grid-size histogram over the 66 contributing gpt2 documents at the production config: {2: 21, 3: 21, 4: 8, 5: 8, 6: 3, 7: 4, 8: 1} -- MAX 8, never 12, and _meta_phd_fit_points_median = 3.0 with _meta_phd_fit_points_min = 2. Twenty-one of 66 documents (32%) contribute a power-law slope through exactly TWO grid points, which has zero residual degrees of freedom and is a finite difference rather than a fit, and 42 of 66 (64%) use two or three. All of them enter phd_dimension's unweighted mean with the same weight as an 8-point fit.

34 of 100 documents contribute nothing to the headline at the shipped corpus and config (17 too short, 17 ungriddable), so phd_dimension is a mean over the long tail of the corpus rather than over the corpus. The warning fires (threshold 10%), which is right, but the reported value is still labelled as if it were the corpus mean.

The per-document path still uses `_mx = min(max_points, _doc.shape[0])` with max_points = the 2000 CLOUD cap, where the pooled path uses `eff_max = min(phd_max_points, n_cloud)` with phd_max_points = 512. They coincide only because max_length = 512 truncates every document; set max_length above 512 (the knob exists) and the two paths silently use different candidate-size ceilings again. This was reported last round and not fixed.

The per-document path yields nothing when dataset is None (`samples = []`), so a dataset=None call silently reports the POOLED estimate under the name phd_dimension. _meta_phd_pooled_fallback is emitted, but the headline column changes estimand.

If _phd_dimension raises for any document, the whole per-text loop is aborted by the outer `except Exception` and the partial per_text list is used -- and in that case the four buckets no longer sum to _n_seen, so the invariant the fix rests on is not enforced on the exception path.
The per-document pass runs its own full forward pass over num_samples documents IN ADDITION to the pooled pass, roughly doubling the task's cost.
fix: Move the accounting INTO the generator: count every document the task was configured to see and add explicit `empty_text` / `no_hidden_states` buckets, so `_meta_phd_n_texts_seen` equals num_samples and the sum invariant covers the drops that happen before the cloud exists. Weight the per-document mean by the number of grid points (or require a minimum of 3-4 and count the rest as a fifth bucket) -- 32% of contributing documents are two-point slopes. Pass phd_max_points, not max_points, as the per-document ceiling. Correct the '4 points ... 12 points' sentence to the measured histogram {2:21, 3:21, 4:8, 5:8, 6:3, 7:4, 8:1}.
